title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
prompt: You are given an integer array `nums`, sorted in ascending order with distinct values, that has been rotated at some unknown pivot. Given the array and an integer `target`, return the index of `target` if it exists in `nums`, or `-1` if it does not. Your algorithm must run in `O(log n)` time.
constraints: All values of nums are unique
nums is an ascending array possibly rotated at an unknown pivot
hints: A plain linear scan works but is O(n) — the sorted structure (even rotated) allows O(log n).
At any midpoint, at least one of the two halves (left of mid, or right of mid) is guaranteed to be normally sorted. Figure out which half is sorted by comparing nums[low] to nums[mid].
Once you know which half is sorted, check whether target falls within that sorted half's range; if so, search there, otherwise search the other half. Repeat until found or the search space is empty.

solution.approach: Use a modified binary search. At each step, one of the two halves split by mid is guaranteed to be in normal sorted order. Determine which half is sorted by comparing nums[lo] to nums[mid]. If the left half is sorted and target falls within nums[lo]..nums[mid), search left; otherwise search right. Symmetrically, if the right half is sorted, check whether target falls within nums[mid+1]..nums[hi], and search accordingly. This discards half the search space each iteration, giving O(log n) time.
